title: anomaly-annotation-proto-and-explainers
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a lightweight, operator-first annotation protocol for anomalies detected in the inference stack and a set of compact "explainers" (linked artifacts) that are surfaced from dashboards. The goal is to: speed triage, create structured context for postmortems, and feed automated quality/feature signals back into model rollouts and Optimize suggestions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers inference-layer anomalies (latency spikes, token-cost regressions, hallucination/quality regression alerts, high error-rate traces).
- Assumes traces and metrics are already collected with request and session ids, model variant id, tenant id, and route metadata.
- Lightweight: annotations are short, searchable, and link to deeper artifacts rather than embedding everything.
- Integrates with existing tooling: dashboard event stream, trace viewer, and our incident tracker.

Annotation schema (recommended minimal fields):
- annotation_id: short unique id (auto, e.g. ann-20250108-013)
- detected_at: ISO timestamp when annotation created
- detected_by: alert | synthetic | operator | probe | canary
- severity: sev1 | sev2 | sev3 | note
- summary: one-line human summary
- suspected_root: list of short tags (kvcache-evict, batching-regression, model-variant, network-blip, cold-start, quantization-error)
- impacted_scope: list (tenant_ids or cohort descriptors or percentage estimate)
- primary_trace: trace_url or trace_id (single span that best represents the anomaly)
- metric_refs: list of metric series ids used to detect the anomaly (latency.p50, error.rate, token.cost)
- explainer_links: list of urls (model-diff, prompt-replay, token-attribution, embedding-compare)
- suggested_action: free text (canary rollback, increase-batching, restart-pool, escalate-sre)
- linked_ticket: incident/JIRA id if raised
- operator_notes: free text (what was tried, outcomes)

Format example (CSV-like single-line example for quick ingestion):
annotation_id,detected_at,detected_by,severity,summary,suspected_root,impacted_scope,primary_trace,metric_refs,explainer_links,suggested_action,linked_ticket,operator_notes
ann-20250108-013,2025-01-08T04:12:19Z,alert,sev2,"spike: p95 latency 4s for route /generate","kvcache-evict;fallback-small-model","tenant:acme-inc;~2% requests","trace:abc123","latency.p95.route.generate;kvcache.evictions","https://replay.redwood.ai/replays/abc123;https://model-diff/compare/xyz","restart-kv-pool;increase-provisioned-cache",JIRA-789,"cold-start pattern post-deploy; operator warmed cache and p95 fell to 300ms"

Dashboard UX suggestions (compact panels and where to surface annotations):
- Event stream panel: chronological event feed (annotations) with lightweight badges for severity and suspected_root. Click expands into a small sidecar with primary_trace and explainer_links.
- Heatmap panel: tenancy heatmap for anomaly density (annotation events) over last 72h. Tooltip shows annotation summary and link to event detail.
- Trace anchor panel: shows a short list of anchors (span ids) for recent annotations; each anchor includes token-attribution link and a miniature cost delta bar.
- Explainer sidecar: small panel that can surface 3 types of explainer artifacts inline: prompt-replay, token-delta histogram, and model-output-diff. Each explainer has a single-line synopsis.

Suggested minimal explainer artifacts (best-effort auto-generated):
1) Prompt-replay URL: replay the request/response and allow switching model versions.
2) Token-attribution snapshot: top-10 tokens contributing to latency or cost (delta vs baseline).
3) Variant-output-diff: small diff of top-k outputs from baseline model vs current model (text + token-level highlight).
4) Metric-sparkline with context: 24h mini-sparkline of the metric that fired with annotation markers.

Automated generation rules (heuristic examples):
- When a latency alert triggers with an attached trace id, auto-create an annotation with detected_by=alert, severity mapped, primary_trace linked, and auto-populated metric_refs. Add explainer_links if the trace contains model-output or request payload.
- For canary regression detectors, include a variant-output-diff explainer automatically if paired eval prompts exist in the canary run.

Triage decision matrix (operator-first):
- sev1 (system outage or >50% errors across many tenants): immediate page, create incident ticket, annotation created by paging system with suggested_action: run rollback/fallback policy.
- sev2 (localized high-latency / quality regression affecting small cohort): create annotation, link trace, open quick canary rollback PR if present, run prompt-replay to validate regression.
- sev3 / note (single-tenant blip, synthetic probe degredation): annotate, set monitoring watch, no immediate rollback unless repeated.

Investigation quickchecks (copy-paste checklist):
- confirm trace contains model-variant id and token counts
- check kvcache eviction events in trace (span tag: kvcache.eviction=true)
- compare model-variant token-cost for sample requests (explainer: token-delta)
- run prompt-replay against baseline variant and current variant (quick sanity compare)
- check recent deployment or autoscale events near detected_at

Operator playbook snippets (commands & queries to help fill annotation):
- traces: retrieveTrace(traceId) -> get span list and model tags
- metrics: SELECT p95, p50 FROM latency WHERE route = '/generate' and tenant IN (...) GROUP BY timeframe
- prompt replay: replayService.fetch(replayId) -> open sidecar

Annotation lifecycle and signals back into product:
- annotations should be searchable (by suspected_root, tenant, metric_refs)
- weekly digest: transform annotations into a weekly CSV for product/research to prioritize model/infra fixes
- integrate high-confidence suspected_root labels into Optimize recommendations (eg: if many annotations tag kvcache-evict, propose increased cache or different eviction policy)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How do we surface annotation privacy concerns? some traces include PII; need automatic scrubbers or redact link previews.
- Do we allow freeform tags or a constrained list for suspected_root? constrained lists are easier to aggregate but less flexible.
- UX: inline explainer thumbnail vs opening full panel — availability of real estate in dashboards.
- telemetry: how many annotations are auto-generated vs operator-created? track and report.

Example short narrative (walkthrough):
1) synthetic probe flags p95 spike for route /embed at 12:01 UTC.
2) alert auto-creates annotation ann-20250108-033 with severity sev2 and links to primary trace.
3) operator opens event stream, clicks explainer sidecar -> sees prompt-replay and token-attribution showing token delta concentrated in user-prepended context.
4) operator notes suspected_root=kvcache-evict, escalates to infra with suggested_action=restart-kv-pool and files JIRA-901.
5) infra restarts pool; operator updates annotation operator_notes: "restart completed; p95 returned to baseline in 18m".

Appendix: short glossary (operator-friendly):
- explainer: a thin artifact (URL + short synopsis) that helps answer WHY this anomaly matters (eg: model-diff, token-delta, prompt-replay).
- anchor trace/span: a span selected by signal as representative for an anomaly (best single point to start triage).
- suspected_root: preliminary hypothesis tag (not final RCA).

If this looks reasonable I will prototype the annotation UI card (mockup) and a small backend endpoint to accept /annotations.create (minimal JSON) and wire it into the alerting pipeline. Next steps: discuss constrained suspected_root taxonomy in next obs sync, then add PII redaction checklist to proto.

Notes: this is intentionally compact. Want feedback from SRE and Product on the explainer set (what artifacts are highest value).
